title: Chrome Hummingbird: Three Worlds in Fifteen Seconds
prompt:
integrated_multimodal_description: Photorealistic premium science-fiction cinema, shot on a large-format anamorphic lens with deep blacks, precise highlights, realistic materials, physically coherent motion, restrained teal-and-amber grading, subtle film grain, and no visible text. A palm-sized origami hummingbird made from mirror-polished chrome is the single continuous hero subject across all three shots. [Shot 1] In a dark liquid-glass laboratory, an extreme macro shot begins on the dormant chrome hummingbird standing on a black reflective table. At 00:00.700, hairline cyan energy races through its folded seams. Its eye opens, its layered metal feathers unfold one by one, and its wings accelerate from delicate individual clicks into a powerful blur. The camera performs a slow 120-degree clockwise arc and gentle push-in while reflections and shallow depth of field remain physically consistent. [Shot 2] At 00:05.000, on the first heavy musical beat, the hummingbird launches straight past the lens and the camera whip-pans into a fast stabilized chase behind it through a rain-soaked neon megacity canyon at night. It banks tightly between moving vehicles and glass towers; raindrops bead, streak, and scatter from its chrome wings, neon reflections travel correctly across its body, and the camera maintains the same recognizable bird design without morphing. [Shot 3] At 00:10.000, the hummingbird punches upward through the storm cloud ceiling into a vast golden sunrise above the clouds. The camera cranes and arcs around it in one majestic motion as thousands of tiny luminous chrome feathers peel outward into the silhouette of a colossal phoenix, circle once with believable momentum, then flow back together into the original hummingbird hovering perfectly still before the sun at 00:14.500. End on one crisp symmetrical hero frame. No people, dialogue, narration, captions, subtitles, logos, watermarks, letters, or readable symbols.

overall_soundscape: Native stereo sound follows the camera and action precisely: a low laboratory electrical hum, delicate left-to-right metallic feather clicks, a rapidly intensifying wing buzz, a sharp launch whoosh crossing the stereo field, heavy rain and distant thunder in the city, droplets striking metal, then open high-altitude wind and bright crystalline reassembly chimes. No voices or speech.

non_diegetic_music: An original cinematic hybrid score begins as a restrained sub-bass pulse with glass harmonics, adds driving orchestral percussion exactly at 00:05.000, expands into brass and choir-like synthesizer textures at 00:10.000, then resolves with one enormous clean impact and a long shimmering tail at 00:14.500.
research_basis: The supplied H3 review transcript highlights the 15-second ceiling, cinema-grade audiovisual output, stronger consistency than raw action speed, and the need for intentional shot planning.
Official MiniMax H3 prompt guide: integrated multimodal scene description plus overall soundscape and non-diegetic music.
Official ComfyUI H3 workflow: 24 fps, 20 steps, res_multistep sampler, native stereo audio, and 17k+5 frame alignment.
The 1280x736 official 0.9 MP canvas is center-cropped to exact 1280x720 without upscaling.
A single hero subject and explicit timed cuts reduce identity drift while demonstrating instruction following and camera motion.
